characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy focuses on demonstrating that platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity solutions are technically viable. It controls the scope and direction of demonstrator development, aiming to provide concrete evidence supporting policy changes. Success is measured by the credibility and security of the demonstrators, as well as their ability to meet relevant standards like FIDO2 and OpenID Connect. Key metrics include successful authentication against simulated environments and positive external security reviews.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy strongly supports the Policy Advocacy Strategy by providing tangible evidence to back up policy proposals. Demonstrators built under this lever directly inform and strengthen the Procurement Influence Strategy by showcasing feasible alternatives to platform-dependent solutions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: A broad Technical Feasibility Strategy, such as exploring blockchain-anchored identities, could dilute resources and conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy if it alienates more conservative stakeholders. Focusing on niche technologies might also hinder Procurement Influence Strategy if solutions are perceived as impractical.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy shapes the narrative around Denmark's digital identity infrastructure, aiming to influence procurement decisions and promote platform-neutral standards. It controls the arguments presented to policymakers and stakeholders, with the objective of reframing the issue as a matter of resilience, continuity, and supplier concentration risk. Success is measured by the inclusion of platform-neutral language in relevant policy documents and procurement requirements.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy works in synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy, as a broader coalition allows for a more diverse and impactful advocacy position. It also amplifies the Procurement Influence Strategy by creating a favorable policy environment for platform-neutral solutions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Focusing too heavily on privacy arguments within the Policy Advocacy Strategy could conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if it leads to solutions that are technically complex or less secure. Prioritizing open-source governance might also constrain the Procurement Influence Strategy if it limits vendor participation.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy aims to create a broad base of support for platform-neutral digital identity solutions. It controls the composition and engagement of the coalition, with the objective of amplifying advocacy efforts and increasing political pressure for change. Success is measured by the size and diversity of the coalition, as well as its ability to influence policy and procurement decisions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy directly enhances the Policy Advocacy Strategy by providing a stronger and more unified voice. A robust coalition also strengthens the Procurement Influence Strategy by demonstrating broad support for platform-neutral solutions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Building a very broad coalition could conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if diverse stakeholders demand technically complex or conflicting solutions. Actively recruiting dissenting voices might also hinder the Policy Advocacy Strategy if it creates internal divisions and weakens the overall message.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy focuses on incorporating platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements into AltID procurement documents. It controls the specific language and criteria used in procurement processes, aiming to reduce long-term dependency on Apple and Google. Success is measured by the inclusion of relevant language in official procurement documents and the selection of vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy is directly supported by the Policy Advocacy Strategy, which creates a favorable policy environment for platform-neutral procurement. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy, which provides concrete evidence that platform-neutral solutions are viable.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Advocating for very specific requirements within the Procurement Influence Strategy could conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if those requirements are technically challenging or costly to implement. Focusing on a 'digital sovereignty bonus' might also constrain the Coalition Building Strategy if it alienates vendors who rely on platform technologies.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy aims to influence European Digital Identity Wallet standards to support platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms. It controls the project's engagement with relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, with the objective of aligning Danish advocacy with broader European requirements. Success is measured by the inclusion of relevant language in EU standards and the adoption of platform-neutral principles across Europe.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy complements the Policy Advocacy Strategy by extending the advocacy efforts to the European level. It also reinforces the Procurement Influence Strategy by creating a broader market for platform-neutral solutions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Actively championing a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU framework could conflict with the Coalition Building Strategy if it is perceived as too radical or disruptive by some stakeholders. Aggressive EU engagement might also constrain the Technical Feasibility Strategy if it requires adapting demonstrators to evolving standards.
